info.description:
The main API structure

- `/api/v1beta/` <- Most of the API is nested under here. All of the resources there are scoped to what is accessible by the authenticated identity.
- `/api/v1beta/me` <- Everything under this path is scoped to the subject of the authenticated identity.
This means that the identity may be authorized to view more resources, but this is the default view for them.
E.g. the chats route scoped under there will only list the chats created by the user, but the user may be authorized to also view chats shared by other users.

This exhaustively walks the Microsoft Graph drive discovery surfaces that are
relevant for the current user:
- `GET /me/drive`: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/drive-get
- `GET /me/drives`, `GET /groups/{id}/drives`, `GET /sites/{id}/drives`:
  https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/drive-list

- `GET /me/joinedTeams`: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/user-list-joinedteams
- `GET /sites?search=*`: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/site-search

  and `resourceProvisioningOptions` properties:
  https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/group
  https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/group-set-options
- Search requests discover matching group-backed libraries with
  `GET /groups?$search="displayName:..."&$top=20` plus
  `ConsistencyLevel: eventual` before fetching `GET /groups/{id}/drives`:
  https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/search-query-parameter

post.summary:
Store a persistent decision for a tool from the settings surface. The
in-stream ApproveAlways decision remains the other writer of the same rows;
this endpoint exists so a grant flipped back to the policy default in
settings can be re-granted without waiting for the next in-chat approval
stop, and so a tool can be put on ask or denied outright. The
`allow_always` policy only guards grants: it exists to keep the product
from becoming more permissive, and a denial is strictly more restrictive,
so it works in deployments that never enable approvals at all. An ask
needs the approval gate to have any effect, so it is refused without one.

The previous message ID to anchor chat history context.
Preferred over `previous_message_id` for new clients.

chat_provider_id.description: Optional chat provider ID to use for token estimation. If not provided, uses the default provider.

existing_chat_id.description: The ID of an existing chat to use. If provided, the chat with this ID will be used instead of creating a new one.

oneOf.description: File content inputs to include in the estimation.

input_files_ids.description: The IDs of any files attached to this message. These files must already be uploaded to the file_uploads table.

oneOf.description: Configuration for estimating a new chat context.

new_message_content.description:
Content for the new message being composed.
Preferred over `user_message` for new clients.

previous_message_id.description: The ID of the message that this message is a response to. If this is the first message in the chat, this should be empty.

selected_facet_ids.description: IDs of facets selected by the user for this estimation.

system_prompt.description: Additional system prompt content to include in the estimation.
system_prompt.example: You are a concise legal assistant.

virtual_files.description:
Inline file payloads to include in the estimation without persisting
them. Used by clients (e.g. the Outlook add-in) that want to count
transient content — the previewed email body — toward the token budget
without writing a `file_uploads` row that would later orphan if the
user dismissed the preview. Each entry is parsed in-place and included
in the response's `file_details` alongside any `input_files_ids`.

file_details.description: Detailed token usage for each file

TokenUsageResponseFileItem.description: Token usage details for an individual file

filename.description: The original filename of the file

id.description: The unique ID of the file

token_count.description: Number of tokens used for this file's content

TokenUsageStats.description: Token usage statistics for the request

chat_provider_id.description: The chat provider ID that was used for this estimation

file_tokens.description: Number of tokens in file contents

history_tokens.description: Number of tokens in previous messages (chat history)

max_tokens.description: The configured model's maximum token limit

remaining_tokens.description: Remaining tokens available for the model response

total_tokens.description: Total number of tokens in the request

user_message_tokens.description: Number of tokens in the user message

TokenUsageVirtualFile.description:
Inline file content (not persisted) included in a token estimate. The
server decodes the base64 payload, runs the same parser the upload route
uses, tokenizes the result, and discards the bytes once the response is
sent. Per-file size cap matches the upload endpoint's
`max_upload_size_bytes` config.

base64.description: Standard base64 (RFC 4648) of the raw file bytes.

content_type.description:
Provided MIME type. Normalized via the same fallback rules as
`/me/files` (e.g. `application/octet-stream` for `.eml` becomes
`message/rfc822`).

filename.description: Original filename (used for content-type fallback and tokenizer header).

ToolAllowedBy.description: What let an MCP call run without asking the user.

ToolApprovalAnnotations.description:
Snapshot of the MCP annotations used to decide whether a tool call needs
user approval. The values are normalized to the MCP defaults so an absent
annotation remains auditable as the pessimistic interpretation.

ToolApprovalDecision.description:
Decision submitted for a generation stopped at an MCP approval gate.

`RejectAlways` needs no policy flag the way `ApproveAlways` needs
`allow_always`: a denial is more restrictive than anything the policy does.

ToolApprovalKind.description:
Which surface a durable approval stop belongs to. `McpTool` is the
default so rows written before the other kinds existed keep parsing.

ToolArgumentKind.description: How the readable view shows one argument.

ToolArgumentNode.description:
One argument in the readable view. A member's name is the last segment of
its path; the value is read from `input` at `path`. Both are raw: the
reader unescapes the segment and cleans and caps both like other server text.

children.description: A group's members or a list's entries, in argument order.

machine_name.description: The member's own name is a machine identifier, which a card does not show.

omitted.description: Members or entries left out of `children`.

path.description: A JSON pointer into `input`; the empty pointer is the whole input.

ToolCallAction.description: What a call does. Reads, and anything none of the verbs fits, are `other`.

fields.description: What each field does across the rows, the first ones the batch writes.

operations.description: Rows per operation, when rows name their own.

read_all.description: Every row was read. Only then may a card say what no row does.

rows.description: The first rows, deletions first, each with its number in the call.

rows_removing_from_lists.description: Rows that remove items from a list, on the tool's word.

same_change.description: Every row writes the same values, ignoring what identifies a row.

shared.description: The one change every row makes, when `same_change`.

ToolCallBatchField.description: What one field does across all of a batch's rows.

distinct.description: How many different values the rows write.

lists_added.description: Rows whose list the tool says has its items added.

lists_removed.description: Rows whose list the tool says has its items removed.

samples.description: The first different values, as examples.

effects_omitted.description: Fields of the row past the cap, which the card counts.

name.description: What it is called; absent when only a machine ID identifies it.

name_from_earlier.description: `name` came from an earlier result naming a machine ID, not the call.

number.description: The row's position in the call, from 1.

ToolCallChange.description:
What a call changes, described the same way for every server and computed
by code from the call's real arguments next to its label: what each value
does, how far it reaches, what is lost, and what the card cannot know.
Shown only: it never decides whether a call needs approval.

complete.description:
Every value was read and classified. Only then may a card state what
the part it does not show cannot hold.

consent_left_out.description: The call set an approval value of its own, which is left out.

effects.description:
Every value the call writes, in the call's order. Capped; `counts`
counts them all, and `complete` says whether everything was read.

filter.description:
Which records or which part of one the call applies to: a filter, or
the values beside content the call marks new, such as a heading.

flags.description: Boolean arguments that change what the call does; only those set.

opaque.description: Content the card cannot read: SQL, shell, code or an instruction.

opaque_omitted.description: Statements past the cap, which the card counts.

place.description:
Where the record lives when no target says so, such as its project
or repository, joined when the call names several; never its table.

record_unread.description:
The one record the call acts on is named only by a machine ID that no
result in this chat held, every result read whole: a card says the
record was not read here and where its ID is.

table.description:
The table or type the record is one of, as the call names it, when
that says more than the label's kind: a card reads it as part of the
kind ("account row", "Namespace"), never as where the record goes.

texts.description: Long text the call writes, shown as a block.

texts_omitted.description: Long texts past the cap, which the card counts.

ToolCallChangeNote.description:
What a card says in a closed sentence: what the tool claims, always as the
tool's claim, and what nobody can know.

ToolCallEffect.description: One value a call writes and what happens to what is there.

added.description: What a replaced list gains, where an earlier result showed the list.

kept.description: What a replaced list keeps, where an earlier result showed the list.

link.description: The value only links to another record.

list.description: The value is a list, whichever effect it has.

new_name.description:
A name the call gives a record nobody read in this chat (see
`record_unread`): a card reads it as a new value, never as the name of
the record being changed.

old.description: The value an earlier result in the chat showed; absent when unknown.

raw_name.description: The member as written, display-cleaned; the card shows it under see more.

removed.description: What a replaced list loses, where an earlier result showed the list.

values.description: The new value, or a list's new values; empty when the value is emptied.

ToolCallEffectCounts.description: How many values a call writes, by effect, including those past the caps.

ToolCallEffectKind.description: What happens to a value, ranked from most to least to lose.

ToolCallEffectValue.description: One value as a card shows it.

machine_id.description: A machine identifier: the card shows `text`, or a phrase when it is empty.

meaning.description:
What a coded value (`text`, as written) stands for, where the
operator's glossary, the tool's own schema or an earlier result says so.

text.description:
Display-cleaned and capped. For a machine identifier: the name of the
record it stands for, or empty when no result names it.

ToolCallFailure.description: How a call failed when Erato, not the tool, wrote its error.

ToolCallFilter.description: What a filter selects, in words.

every_record.description: The filter is empty: every record.

omitted.description: Conditions past the cap, which the card counts.

is_empty.description: The condition asks for an empty value.

dry_run.description: It asks for a dry run: the call says what it would do without doing it.

ToolCallLabel.description:
What a tool call does to what, and where, read from its arguments by code.
The verb and the kind come from closed lists, never from argument text, and
every value keeps the pointer it was read through. Shown only: it never
decides whether a call needs approval or which decisions a card offers.

arguments.description:
The arguments for the generic card: paths into the call's `input` and
how to show each, never the values themselves.

change.description:
What the call changes, in the same terms on every server. Absent on
older rows, labels with no verb and labels written by hand, which
render as before.

items.description: What the call acts on; empty on a `generic` label.

ToolCallLabelItem.description: One thing a call acts on, each part read through its own pointer.

fields.description: Key values worth showing, each with its argument's `name`.

target.description: Where the item goes or lives: a parent, folder, channel or recipient.

ToolCallLabelSlot.description: The values one pointer reached in a call's arguments.

name.description: The argument's name, display-cleaned; set on fields.

omitted.description: Values the pointer reached beyond those kept.

pointer.description:
A JSON pointer into the call's `input` where `*` stands for every
element. A lookup key, never shown.

ToolCallLabelSource.description: Who chose a label's pointers. Values are always read by code.

ToolCallLabelValue.description: One value as the call wrote it.

machine_id.description:
A machine identifier (see `tool_display::label::machine_id`): a card
never shows `text`, only `resolved` if a name is known, and Technical
details keeps it.

path.description: Where the value sits in `input`, with indices in place of `*`.

resolved.description:
What earlier results in the chat say about this value, never what the
call itself says: on `id`, `target` and `before` the name of the record
the value identifies; on a field of an update, the value the field held
in the record the item's `id` names, where an earlier link shows as its
record's name and never as a raw ID. Absent when no result has it.

text.description: Display-cleaned and capped; an object reads as compact JSON.

ToolCallLabelWarning.description: Something the card says next to a label.

ToolCallObjectKind.description: What kind of thing a call acts on.

ToolCallOpaque.description: Content whose effect only reading it could tell.

found.description:
Risky words found in it, as written in the closed lists. Findings
only: never the verb.

text.description: Its start, display-cleaned; the card reads the rest from `input`.

write_inside_read.description: A write found in a statement that opens like a read.

kind.description: To, copy or blind copy, in words a card can say.

values.description: Every address as written, capped; machine IDs are counted, not listed.

ToolCallRecipientKind.description: How a group of recipients is addressed.

ToolCallRecipients.description: Who a call reaches. Group addresses count as one and are never expanded.

groups.description: One group per recipient member: to, cc, bcc and the like.

outside.description: Addresses outside the organisation, as written.

outside_known.description: Whether `outside` was computed: the signed-in user's domain is known.

unchecked.description: Recipients with no address to check, such as a number or an ID.

before.description: The text it replaces, where the call says.

text.description: Its start, display-cleaned; the card reads the rest from `input`.

ToolCallValueMeaning.description: What a coded value stands for, and whose word that is.

ToolCallValueMeaningSource.description:
Whose word a value's meaning is; a card marks every meaning but the
glossary's as the tool's claim, an earlier result's included.

ToolDisplayMetadata.description:
Inert display text for a tool call, captured with the call: the tool
descriptor's text, the server's name and the call's label. Never used to
select a tool, evaluate policy or execute a call.

label.description:
What this call does to what, and where. Absent on client tools and
older rows, which render as before.

read_only.description:
Whether the tool is read-only by the annotations the approval policy
read for this call and does not also call itself destructive. Set on
MCP calls only.

server_name.description:
The MCP server as the operator named it, else its id tidied up; never
text from the server itself. Absent on client tools and older rows.

ToolResultDetails.description:
What a tool row keeps of an MCP result besides `output`: at most ten of its
links. Its structured content and embedded resources are not kept.

failure.description:
Set by Erato when a call failed without an answer from the tool that
Erato could read: the row's error text is then Erato's, never the
tool's.

ToolResultLink.description:
A resource link from the result. Only `https` links with a host, without
user info and at most 512 bytes long are kept; the name and title are
display-cleaned and capped like a tool title.

host.description:
The link's host as the URL parser reads it: lowercase, and punycode for
a non-ASCII name, so a lookalike host reads as `xn--…`.

matches_server_host.description:
Whether `host` is the host of the MCP server's configured URL, ignoring
case and port. Never true for a server without a URL.

oneOf.description:
Why an MCP call ran without an approval card. Absent when the user
decided on a card, the call was refused, on other tools and old rows.

Set on MCP calls, label included and description left out: only
approval cards show that.

The links of an MCP result. For the UI only: replay drops it, so the
model never sees it.
At a local date and time.

allOf.description: On a repeating schedule.

oneOf.description: On a repeating schedule.

Trigger.description:
What makes an item happen. Times are local to the zone stored with the
item; event-driven triggers will be further variants.

UnarchiveChatResponse.description: Response from the unarchive chat endpoint

chat_id.description: The ID of the unarchived chat

UpdateAssistantRequest.description: Request to update an existing assistant

description.description: Optional new description for the assistant

enforce_facet_settings.description: Optional new enforcement flag for assistant facet settings

facet_ids.description: Optional new list of facet IDs for this assistant

file_ids.description: Optional list of file upload IDs to associate with this assistant

mcp_server_ids.description: Optional new list of MCP server IDs

name.description: Optional new name for the assistant

prompt.description: Optional new prompt for the assistant

allOf.description: The updated assistant with files

UpdateChatRequest.description: Request to update mutable chat fields.

disabled_mcp_server_ids.description:
MCP servers to switch off for this chat; replaces the stored list.
Their tools are withheld from the model. Only ever narrows the set the
policy, assistant and facets allow.

disabled_mcp_tools.description:
`server/tool` patterns of MCP tools to switch off for this chat;
replaces the stored list. Matching tools are withheld from the model.
Only ever narrows the set the policy, assistant, facets and the
server list allow; a pattern naming a tool the server no longer
exposes does nothing.

is_pinned.description: Whether the chat should be pinned.

mcp_write_tools_enabled.description:
Whether the model may be offered MCP write tools and client actions
in this chat. Off, only tools the server marks read-only are offered
and client-action proposals are withheld.

title_by_user_provided.description:
Optional user-provided title update.
- `\"some title\"` sets the title
- `null` removes a previously set title
- omitted is treated the same as `null`

chat_id.description: The ID of the updated chat

disabled_mcp_server_ids.description: MCP servers the user switched off for this chat.

disabled_mcp_tools.description: `server/tool` patterns of MCP tools the user switched off for this chat.

is_pinned.description: Whether the chat is pinned by its owner.

mcp_write_tools_enabled.description:
Whether the model may be offered MCP write tools and client actions
in this chat.

title_by_summary.description: Title of the chat as generated by summary automation.

title_by_user_provided.description: Title of the chat as explicitly provided by the user.

title_resolved.description: Resolved chat title where user-provided title takes precedence over summary title.

client_tool_decisions.description: Replaces all per-tool client tool decisions, keyed by qualified `namespace/name`.

preference_assistant_additional_informat.description: Additional contextual information about the user for the assistant.

preference_assistant_custom_instructions.description: Additional behaviour/style/tone preferences for the assistant.

preference_default_chat_provider.description: Preferred default chat provider/model ID for new chats.

preference_language.description: The client's UI language as a BCP 47 tag, reported like the time zone.

preference_nickname.description: Preferred name to address the user with.

preference_starting_assistant_cleared.description:
Set `true` to explicitly clear the start screen (welcome screen even
though an audience pin exists), `false` to inherit again. Clearing
also removes any own pick; picking also un-clears.

preference_starting_assistant_id.description:
The user's own start-screen pick when it is an assistant that was never
published to the hub, as an `assistants.id`. Setting either pick field
removes the other.

preference_starting_hub_assistant_id.description:
The user's own start-screen pick when it is a hub assistant, as an
`assistant_hub_assistants.id` (NOT the clone's `assistants.id` — those
go stale on every hub republish). Explicit `null` removes the pick and
returns to inheriting any audience pin.

preference_time_zone.description:
The client's IANA time zone (the browser's
`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`). Clients report it
when it differs from the profile's `preference_time_zone`; anything
that is not an IANA zone name is rejected with 422.

client_tool_decisions.description: Per-tool decisions keyed by qualified `namespace/name`; absent tools keep their default.

client_tool_file_approval.description: Effective decision, including the configured default when no user override exists.

email.description: The user's email address. Shouldn't be used as a unique identifier, as it may change.

groups.description:
List of groups the user belongs to.

Derived from the ID token's `groups` claim, or Microsoft Graph for Entra overage.

organization_group_ids.description:
Organization membership IDs from the token or Entra overage resolution.

These can be used as subject_id when creating share grants
with subject_id_type "organization_group_id".

organization_user_id.description:
Organization user ID from the `oid` claim (Entra ID specific).

This can be used as the subject_id when creating share grants
with subject_id_type "organization_user_id".

preference_assistant_additional_informat.description: Additional contextual information about the user for the assistant.

preference_assistant_custom_instructions.description: Additional behaviour/style/tone preferences for the assistant.

preference_default_chat_provider.description: The user's preferred default chat provider/model ID.

preference_language.description:
The language (BCP 47) the user's client last reported, used for
messages Erato sends later, such as reminders.

preference_nickname.description: Preferred name to address the user with.

preference_starting_assistant_cleared.description:
True when the user explicitly cleared their start screen. This is
deliberately distinct from "never set": a clear must keep suppressing
an admin's audience pin, while "never set" inherits it.

preference_starting_assistant_id.description:
The user's own start-screen pick when it is an assistant that was never
published to the hub, stored as an `assistants.id`. At most one of the
two pick fields is ever set.

preference_starting_hub_assistant_id.description:
The user's own start-screen pick when it is a hub assistant, stored as
an `assistant_hub_assistants.id` — stable across hub republishes, unlike
the clone's `assistants.id`. The LIVE assistant id it points at is
resolved per request by `GET /me/starting-assistant`.

preference_time_zone.description:
The IANA time zone the user's client last reported (web app or
Teams). Local times the user enters, such as a reminder's date and
time, are resolved in it.

preferred_language.description:
The user's preferred language.

The final determined language is intersected with our supported languages, to determine the final language.

Will be a BCP 47 language tag (e.g. "en" or "en-US").

This is derived in the following order (highest priority first):
- `i18n.language.language_detection_priority`
- Default language from `i18n.language.default_language`
- "en"

oneOf.description: `null` deactivates the tool's decision, back to the policy default.

UserToolDecision.description:
A user's persistent decision for one MCP tool. Rows exist only while a
decision is active; the absence of a row means the policy default applies.
